Priority #3 for increased HE loads and device sizes 26 DCX STRATEGY DCX Increase the Quality and Quantity of Data Generated at DARHT Multi-image radiography has proven to be one of the highest priorities for the weapon design community and mul- tiple efforts are underway to further this capability at DARHT. This section describes a number of areas planned for enhancements and includes: (1) efforts to advance the GRCs, enabling higher radiographic performance and increas- ing the number of images; (2) non-radiographic complementary diagnostics, data analysis, and data management; (3) the addition of a MPTL to enable research in beam–target interactions to advance the technical readiness level of x-ray conversion targets; and (4) improvements to DARHT A2 and concepts for extending viewing axes. The impetus behind many of the proposed mechanical systems advancements outlined throughout this section is to design uni- versal mechanical systems and parts (e.g., Bucky grids, scintillators, cameras, lenses, alignment stands, mounting structures, etc.) that will be interoperable between DARHT and ASD/Scorpius. Advancements will also ideally realize benefits beyond just DARHT and ASD/Scorpius, mitigating operational risk within the weapons program. Gamma Ray Cameras and Radiography Fundamental and critical technology to DARHT are the GRCs that image the imploding object illuminated by the x-rays from A1 and A2. This is essentially the principal measurement for DARHT.
